rationale: C01 is a highly plausible drafting template. It concerns an Atomic Energy Commission labor dispute, uses nearly the same two-recital structure and national-safety finding, and reproduces the child's entire operative sequence: Title II powers and duties, a section 206 reporting deadline, and continued Board existence until presidential termination. C14 is similarly close but differs in referring to national health and safety and only a threatened strike. C23 closely matches the child's realized-strike and national-safety language, but lacks C01's additional Atomic Energy Commission context.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between the Goodyear Atomic Corporation and certain of its employees ... at certain facilities ... of the Atomic Energy Commission
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS there exists a labor dispute between the Union Carbide and Carbon Corporation and certain of its employees ... at certain facilities of the Atomic Energy Commission
shared_material.explanation: The opening recital uses the same specific party-and-facility construction in the Atomic Energy Commission context, with the employer, unions, and locations substituted.

shared_material.child_excerpt: affects a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to continue, will imperil the national safety
shared_material.parent_excerpt: affecting a substantial part of an industry engaged in trade or commerce among the several States or with foreign nations, or in the production of goods for commerce, which strike, if permitted to occur or to continue, will imperil the national safety
shared_material.explanation: The national-emergency finding is nearly verbatim, adapted from a threatened strike to a strike already underway.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before May 15, 1957.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of the said Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the provisions of section 206 of the said Act on or before July 20, 1954.
shared_material.explanation: The operative powers and reporting provision is identical except for the deadline.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Upon submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence to perform such other functions as may be required under the said Act, until the Board is terminated by the President.
shared_material.explanation: The concluding administrative provision is reproduced verbatim.
